title: SQL fund data pipeline
card_detail: SQLite pipeline: staging, rejects, window-function marts and quality checks.
context: A small SQL data pipeline on synthetic fund prices and trades: raw tables, staging with a reject table, marts built with SQL window functions, and automated data-quality checks. Built in October 2026 as a practice project. It uses no real fund or client data, no cloud database and no cash or currency handling.

statement.tool: SQLite and SQL window functions, driven from Python
statement.built: Seven reject rules, positions, time-weighted returns and drawdown marts, six quality checks and 15 tests
statement.result: All 7 injected faults were rejected with the right reason, and the SQL marts matched an independent NumPy calculation to 1e-10 in value

flow_label: Raw load to staging to marts to checks
method_note: Every raw trade ends up either staged or in the reject table with the first rule it broke, so no row disappears silently. The daily return is time-weighted, so contributions are not counted as performance.

plots.label: Fund index
plots.alt: Cumulative performance index of three synthetic funds over 250 business days
plots.caption: Generated output · fund index from the SQL mart

spec: Synthetic prices and trades, fixed seed, three funds, six securities
Positions, fund value, time-weighted return, index, drawdown
Cloud warehouse, cash, currencies, incremental loads
results: 7 injected faults, one per rule, all rejected correctly
max difference 1.2e-10 in value, 4.4e-16 in return
decisions: Rejects are kept in a table with a reason instead of being dropped.
Time-weighted return so that trades do not look like performance.
A second, independent calculation in NumPy to verify the SQL.
verification: 15 tests inject one fault per reject rule, an oversell and a corrupted mart row, check that every raw trade is accounted for, compare the marts with NumPy and rebuild twice to show the load is repeatable.
